lines.text: Morning, Helen. Can you hear me okay? I've got the little bars going up and down so I think it's working.
I can hear you, Priya. A bit of an echo, but it's fine. Is that you or is that me?
Might be me. Let me put the headset on. Hang on.
Take your time. We're still waiting for the others anyway.
Hello, hello. Sorry, am I on mute? I think I'm on mute.
You were, Ben. You're fine now.
Right, good. The button's in a different place on this laptop. I keep hitting the wrong one.
Morning, Ben. We can see you, but you're a bit dark. Is there a light behind you?
It's the window. Let me turn the screen. Is that better?
Much better. Now we can see your face and not just your outline.
That's what my wife says too.
Ha. Raymond's just joined, I think. Raymond, can you hear us?
Yes, yes, I'm here. Sorry. The meeting link took me to the wrong room first, and then I had to log in again.
It does that. Good morning, Raymond.
Morning, all. Can you see my screen? I've got a spreadsheet open and I'm not sharing it, I hope.
No, we just see you. Your camera's pointing a little at the ceiling.
Oh. Is that better? I'm never sure with this stand.
Now we see the top of your head.
Well, that's worse. Hold on. There. Okay.
Lovely. Everyone's here, then. Priya, are you sharing the status page, or shall I just ask you?
I can share it, but I don't think we need it. It's all in my head, honestly. Well, and in the report.
Fine. Let's get going, it's a full agenda and I'd like us to finish on time. Steering: overall status, the licence, the vaccines and power, parking, and the budget.
Sounds good. I'll be listening hardest for the budget bit, you won't be surprised.
I never am. Priya, overall status please.
Overall amber. The cutover is still the thirteenth and fourteenth of February, but three things have no slack left: the licence, the X-ray slot and the handover.
Mm-hm. Okay. Say that again, the three things, so I've got them straight.
The licence, the X-ray slot, and the handover. Those three.
Right. And everything else is where we want it?
Everything else I'd call on track. Those three are the ones where there's nothing in reserve. If they move, the date moves.
Sorry, can I just check, when you say no slack, you mean literally none? Not a little?
Literally none, Raymond. That's why it's amber and not green.
Okay. That's clear. I just wanted to be sure I wasn't reading too much into it.
I'd say amber is fair. I wouldn't call it green, with three of them sitting like that.
Amber is honest. What would make it red?
Any one of those three slipping by more than a week.
Any one. Not all three together, just one of them.
Just one. That's how I've been looking at it.
So it's a fairly tight trigger, then.
It is. But I'd rather say it plainly now than have you hear it later.
Agreed. I'd much rather have it plain. Ben, you're nodding. Anything to add on that?
No, no, I was just agreeing. I think it's a fair description. Mine is mostly the last topic anyway, so I'll hold it.
Okay. Raymond, anything on status before we go on?
Not on status. I'll come back to it in the budget, if that's all right. I just wanted to know what amber means so I can say it properly to the others.
Sure. Amber means the date is holding, but with nothing in reserve on three items. Priya, is that fair?
That's fair. That's the whole message.
Good. Then the licence.
The ministry gave us a date: the licence for the new address will be issued on the sixth of February.
Good, that's a week before the cutover. Is that in writing?
Yes, we have the e-mail from the ministry.
Okay. I only ask because I've been on the wrong end of a verbal date before.
Understood. This one's not verbal. It's written down.
Sorry, just so I follow. The sixth, and then the cutover is the thirteenth. Is that right?
Yes. The sixth is when it's issued, and the cutover is the thirteenth and fourteenth.
Right. So about a week between the two.
A week, yes. Which is why I called it good. But it's also why it's one of the three with no slack, isn't it?
Exactly. A week sounds like a lot, but if the licence slips by more than a week, that's the red trigger we just talked about.
Mm-hm. So the cushion is that week and nothing more.
That's right.
Can I ask, and tell me if it's a silly question. Is the sixth the date they issue it, or the date we receive it?
What the e-mail says is that it will be issued on the sixth. That's the wording I've got.
Okay. Issued. Fine. I just wanted to be sure I had the word right.
Good question, though. The words matter with ministries.
They always do.
Priya, you're comfortable with it? You're not worried about the e-mail?
I'm comfortable that it's in writing. That was the thing I wanted. I can't speak for the ministry beyond what they've told us.
No, of course. That's a fair way to put it.
Sorry, I'm going to go back one step, if I can. On the status, you said the licence, X-ray and handover. Is the licence the one you're most comfortable with now that you have the date?
I wouldn't rank them, Raymond. I'd say the licence now has a date in writing, which is better than before. But it still has no slack, so it's still on the list.
Okay, so it's on the list, but it's better than it was.
Yes. That's a fair way to say it.
I'm happy with that. Let's not spend longer on it. Ben, the vaccine risk.
Backup power for the fridge circuit is now commissioned and tested, so the vaccine risk is much smaller.
Mm-hm. Much smaller. Not gone.
Not gone, no. I wouldn't say gone. I'd say much smaller.
Sorry, Ben, when you say commissioned and tested, is that finished? Like, it's done?
Commissioned and tested, yes. That's what I'm telling you. It's been through both.
Right. I just wanted to hear it in plain words. Thank you.
And that's the fridge circuit specifically.
The fridge circuit, yes. That's the part that matters for the vaccines.
That's a big one to tick off, Ben. I know it's been on everyone's mind.
It has. It's been on mine for a long time, to be honest. So it's a relief.
I can imagine. So where does that leave the vaccine risk, in your words?
Much smaller than it was. That's the honest version. It's not zero, but it's much smaller.
We'll still do the cool box run with loggers, just as a second line of defence.
Right. So belt and braces.
Belt and braces, yes. Second line, that's all.
Is that a case of the backup power not being trusted, or just being careful?
Careful. I trust the backup power, that's why I said much smaller. The cool boxes are there as a second line, in case.
Okay. That makes sense. I wasn't trying to suggest anything, I just wanted to understand the reason.
No, that's fair. It's a reasonable thing to ask.
I think it's the right attitude, frankly. The first line is tested, and the second line is there anyway.
And it fits with what we said at the start, that we'd rather be plain than surprised.
It does. Mm-hm.
Can I just say, from my side, it's good to hear it described as smaller and not as solved. I trust that more.
I'd rather not say solved. If I said solved and then something happened, you'd never believe me again.
Ha. Quite right.
Sorry, small thing. Ben, you said the cool box run is a second line. Is that the right way for me to write it up? Second line, not main plan?
Yes. Second line of defence. The backup power is the main protection, the cool box run sits behind it.
Okay, good. I wanted to get the wording right.
Fine. I think we're clear on that. Anyone want to go back to anything before we move on? Raymond?
Only that I want to be sure I've got the story straight for the people I report to. Amber overall, licence in writing, and vaccine risk much smaller. Is that fair?
That's fair. And with the cool box run still being done as a second line.
Yes, and that. Thank you.
And the three with no slack, don't lose those.
The licence, the X-ray slot and the handover. I've got them written down.
Good. Right, I think that's the first three in good shape. Is everyone still with us, no one lost the connection?
Still here.
Still here, no echo now either.
Here. My camera's still pointing the right way, I think.
It is. Well done, Raymond.
Parking.
Right, yes. This one's been going round for a while, so I'm glad to have something to say on it. Let me just find my note. Sorry, one second.
Take your time. Benjamin, you've got your hand up, or is that you waving at someone?
No, that's me waving at the cat. Sorry. Go on, Priya, I'm listening.
Okay. So the position was that we had a gap, and the gap was twelve. Twelve staff who would've had nowhere to park once we're in the new building.
Twelve spaces short. Yes. That's the number I've had in my head as well.
Good, same number then. And the news is this.
HR agreed to subsidise twelve lots in the public car park next door for six months, which covers the gap of twelve.
Mm-hm. Sorry, just so I have it straight. Twelve lots, and the gap is twelve. So it's one for one?
One for one, yes. Twelve lots against a gap of twelve. That's why I said it covers it.
Right. Good. I only ask because in pharmacy we've been getting questions, and I'd rather give people the right number than a vague one.
What kind of questions, Benjamin?
Mostly just, is it sorted, is it not sorted. People like a straight answer. I think they've been hearing bits of it in the corridor.
Yes, that's how it goes. Everyone hears half a sentence.
Which is fair, because until this week I only had half a sentence myself.
Can I check one thing? The car park is next door. It's the public one, so it's not ours.
Correct, it's the public car park next door. The subsidy is for twelve lots in there.
Okay. And the six months, that's the length of the subsidy, not, I don't know, a trial of something else.
It's the length of the subsidy. Six months. That's what HR agreed, and that's all I've got on it.
Right. I just wanted to be sure I wasn't mixing it up with another timeline.
I don't think there's another one. Is there, Priya?
Not that I'm aware of, no. It's one agreement, twelve lots, six months.
Sorry, going back a second. When you say HR agreed, is that done, or is that agreed in principle?
They've agreed it. That's the word they used, agreed. I'm not going to dress it up as anything more than that, and I'm not going to water it down either.
Fair enough. Agreed is agreed.
I'm happy with agreed. It's a lot better than where we were a few weeks ago.
It is. I'll admit I was a bit nervous about this one.
You weren't the only one. I kept seeing it come up and thinking, here we go.
Ha, same. It felt like the sort of thing that sits there and never moves.
Well, it's moved. Anything else on the parking itself before I sum it up? Raymond?
Only that I'll want to talk about how it's paid for, but I think that's the next item, so I'll hold it.
Yes, hold that, we'll come to it straight after. Benjamin, anything?
No, I'm fine. Well, one small thing. Twelve covers the gap of twelve. So nobody's left over?
Nobody left over, on the numbers we've got. Twelve and twelve.
Lovely. That's what I'll say, then. Twelve lots, next door, six months.
That's a clean way to put it.
Good, so the parking issue is solved, at least for six months.
Yes. For six months. I'd say it just like that.
Mm-hm. I like the 'at least'. It's honest.
I try. Right, I think that's parking. Priya, thank you, that was a useful bit of news to get.
Thanks. I'm relieved to be honest.
Budget, Raymond.
Yes. Hang on, let me get the right sheet up. I've got three tabs open and none of them are the one I want.
We've all been there. Take a moment.
Is that the one with the green column? I always find the green one.
That's the one. Okay, I've got it. Can you all see it, or should I just talk?
I can't see anything yet. Oh, there. Yes. It's a bit small, though.
I'll just talk through it. The sheet's not telling you much that I won't say anyway.
Spend to date is in line. We've used three thousand of the twenty thousand contingency, for the movers.
Three of twenty. Just so I'm clear, that's three thousand used, and the twenty is the whole contingency.
Yes. Twenty thousand is the total contingency. Three thousand is gone, and it went on the movers.
And when you say in line, in line with what? The plan?
In line with what we expected at this point. Nothing's jumped out at me. That's all I mean by it.
Okay. Good. I wasn't trying to catch you out, I just like to know what the words mean.
No, it's a fair question. I use 'in line' a lot and I don't always say what it's in line with.
I do the same with 'on track'. It can mean almost anything.
Ha, it really can. I'm guilty of that one.
So the movers are the three thousand. Is that the only thing that's come out of contingency so far?
As far as the three thousand goes, yes. That's what I've got. Movers, three thousand.
Right. Okay. I just wanted to hear it said plainly.
So, that leaves a fair bit. Seventeen, if I've done it right.
Seventeen thousand, yes. Twenty less three.
Good, my maths is working today.
Mine isn't. I'd have said sixteen and then doubted myself.
Well, we've got Benjamin for the sums. Go on, Raymond. You said you wanted to talk about the parking.
I did. Sorry, I was getting there. It's the obvious follow-on from the last item.
The parking subsidy adds about eight thousand over six months, which I'd also take from contingency.
Sorry, 'about' eight thousand. Is that a firm figure or an estimate?
It's about eight thousand. That's the word I'd use. I'm not going to claim it's more exact than that.
Okay. Understood. I only ask because 'about' can move.
It can. But about eight thousand over the six months is what I'm working to.
And the six months is the same six months Priya just gave us.
Same six months, yes. The twelve lots, the six months, that's what the eight thousand sits on.
Right. That matches what I told you, I think. Twelve lots, six months.
It does. I'm not changing any of it. I'm just putting a cost against it.
So just so I follow. The movers are three thousand, already used. The parking would be about eight thousand more. Both from the same pot.
Both from contingency, yes. That's what I'd suggest.
Mm-hm. And that pot is twenty thousand to begin with.
Twenty thousand to begin with. Yes.
Hold on, let me just say it back, because I want to be sure I've got it. Three thousand's gone on the movers. Parking adds about eight thousand. Both from contingency.
That's it. You've got it.
And you're happy that's the right place for it? I'm not putting words in your mouth.
I am. I said I'd take it from contingency, and I would. I don't see another obvious place for it.
Can I ask why contingency, rather than somewhere else? I'm not against it. I'm just curious how you got there.
Fair. It's because the parking is the kind of thing contingency is there for. It came up and we need it covered. That's how I see it.
Right. That makes sense. I wasn't pushing back, I just wanted the reasoning.
No, no, that's fine. I'd rather you ask.
Can I add something? From my side, the subsidy is what makes the parking work, so if it comes out of contingency, I'm comfortable with that.
Good. Thank you.
I just wanted to say it, so it's on record that I'm not unhappy with it.
Noted. Benjamin, are you comfortable?
I'm comfortable. I think I was just thinking aloud, really. Three used, about eight more. It's fine.
I'd say the same. It's tidy, to be honest.
Okay. Anyone want to go back to anything before I say it? Parking, movers, anything?
Just a quick one. On the movers, the three thousand. That's been spent, not just promised?
It's what we've used. That's how I'd put it. Used, for the movers.
Fine. Thanks. I keep wanting to pin the words down. Sorry.
Don't be sorry. It's useful. Priya?
Nothing from me. Well, only that I'm glad it's a short conversation. I thought the parking might need a longer one.
I did too. So did I, honestly.
It's the benefit of having an actual answer, I suppose.
Ha, yes. It does save time. Right.
Approved, take the parking subsidy from contingency.
Thank you. Understood.
Mm-hm. Good.
Great. Thanks, everyone.
Well, that's a good place to be. I think that's us for the day, and for the year, really. Thanks all, it's been a pleasure.
Thanks, Helen. Thanks, everyone. Goodbye.
Bye all.
Bye, everyone. Take care.
Bye now.
